bug_semantics: MessagePack skip-entire-structure walks nested arrays and maps by recursion and never increments MessagePackReader.Depth or consults MessagePackSecurity.MaximumObjectGraphDepth. In the 2.x/3.x API this is MessagePackReader.TrySkip(): maps/arrays call TrySkipNextMap/TrySkipNextArray, which loop TrySkip() on each child, so a skipped unknown field whose value is a chain of single-element fixarrays/fixmaps grows C# stack frames until an uncatchable StackOverflowException kills the process. Generated/dynamic formatters, IgnoreFormatter, and unknown-key/default branches invoke reader.Skip() during ordinary deserialization of untrusted payloads; UntrustedData does not mitigate because skip does not participate in depth accounting. The same recursion existed earlier as MessagePackBinary.ReadNextBlock (v1 formatters used that to skip unknown members).
flaw_origin: The flawed mechanism is unbounded recursive skip of a complete MessagePack Array/Map graph, including FixArray/FixMap. It was first written on 2017-02-28 in 62700694def68e90f3ff789c4d6f4433191c6c19 as MessagePackBinary.ReadNextBlock: on MessagePackType.Array/Map it reads the header then recursively calls ReadNextBlock for each element (parent ff5c71344f62eec7a53ac20ef1af2b01e0b4cef1 has ReadNext but no ReadNextBlock). Pre-existing ReadNextMap/ReadNextArray (47e0c50f) are not this bug: FixArray/FixMap still used ReadNext1 (header-only), so nested 0x91 chains would not recurse. 91efb454b1b5b36cd84d5ac9444617492803a7be replaced the byte[]+offset reader with MessagePackReader.Skip/ReadNextArray/ReadNextMap that recursively call Skip() for every array/map code including fix*; 790cadd0d943f77127cddbedf472c32f960e6a28 refactored that to TrySkip without changing the recursion. Those are replacement/refactor, not BIC. a145b7cc (2020-01-14) added MaximumObjectGraphDepth for object-graph reads and did not apply it to Skip.
